title: Certify the Nam-tor settings UI for enrollment and PAM opt-in
regenerated_because: The previous revision of this file certified two desktop-specific UIs: a GNOME GTK4 wizard in crate namtor-gnome and a KDE Plasma 6 KCM in crate namtor-kde. The KCM was removed and namtor-gnome was renamed namtor-ui as the single cross-desktop UI, so every KDE claim here described code that no longer exists (main.qml, namtor_kcm.cpp, libnamtorqml.so, Q_PROPERTY/QQC2 annotations, the 18 lib + 3 abi-smoke suites) and the GNOME claims named renamed crates and moved files. One claim was never true at all: no source file in this repository has ever contained the string 'Software fallback in use'. test_release_ledger.sh counts this file as a PASS, so a release was being certified against a deleted desktop module. Every number below is measured, not asserted.
summary: Certification of the single GTK4/libadwaita settings UI (crate namtor-ui) for end-to-end enrollment and PAM opt-in. CI cannot run a clean desktop session, so the CI-testable surface is structural (binaries staged, system-bus usage, install-manifest ownership, accessibility anchors, warning constants, PAM sufficient control, polkit policy) plus the namtor-ui unit suites. Real enrollment with a camera, real PAM toggle against /etc/pam.d, and real authentication against a running PAM stack are human-gated on a desktop VM and recorded below as WITHHELD.

structural: Settings UI binary staged (namtor-enroll-wizard present in target/release, owned by package=ui in install-manifest.toml)
One UI for every desktop: no per-desktop crate, no QML, no KCM; the desktop entry carries no OnlyShowIn and no desktop-specific keys
SYSTEM bus only: 0 Connection::session / session_bus() references across namtor-ui and namtor-client; the sole connection is Connection::system() at crates/namtor-client/src/dbus_client.rs:53
PAM sufficient control: pam-install.sh defaults CONTROL=sufficient; the editor defaults to NamtorControl::Sufficient; pam_namtor maps all errors to PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL (fall-through to password)

privacy_scan.string_registry: UI_STRING_REGISTRY is checked against the source tree rather than a hardcoded file list. The previous list required navigation.rs, deleted in 196d4a4, so the registry kept 31 strings from code that no longer ships; and it could not notice a new component arriving with no entries. Deriving the expectation immediately found components/scan_feedback.rs, whose user-facing strings had never been scanned.

accessibility.scan_guidance_is_announced: components/scan_feedback.rs sets AccessibleRole on the guidance and quality rows so the scan advice reaches a screen reader, not just the display

no_tpm_warning.flag: ProtectionView.is_software_fallback, set at view_model.rs from ProtectionKeyKind::Software
no_tpm_warning.rendering: components/system_status.rs labels the row 'Software (fallback)', adds the warning CSS class, and renders the warning text as AccessibleRole::Alert
no_tpm_warning.note: This was the only genuine coverage hole in the certification. FakeManagerClient::set_protection_status existed with zero callers and every is_software_fallback in the test tree was a hardcoded false, so no test drove ProtectionKeyKind::Software through the presenter: the machine without a TPM, the one that most needs telling, was the untested path. Verified non-vacuous by forcing is_software_fallback to false, which fails two of the three tests.

high_impact_dialog.text: FAR/FRR and real-attack PAD gates remain unmeasured. Enabling face authentication is experimental and not recommended for security-sensitive use.

password_fallback.module_error_mapping: PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL on any daemon/timeout/error -> sufficient -> ignore -> fall through to password module
password_fallback.rhost_refusal: PAM_RHOST set -> refuse (spec 8.2); sshd classified Unsupported
password_fallback.no_fallback_refused: enable_service refuses a stack with no password fallback. Previously it did not: verify_through_includes classified the candidate, which already contained the namtor block, and classify_service short-circuits on has_namtor and returns Safe before evaluating the fallback rule. It now classifies the stock stack.
password_fallback.module_preflight: enable_service refuses to write a block referencing a pam_namtor.so that is not installed, before taking the backup. EditError::ModuleNotFound existed and was mapped to a D-Bus error but was never produced, because resolve_module_path had no callers.

withheld_human_gated.rationale: A clean desktop session cannot be run in CI. The following require a human-gated desktop VM with a real camera, real /etc/pam.d, and a running PAM stack.
scenarios: Real enrollment with a live IR camera (settings surface -> enroll -> capture frames -> review -> commit -> profile appears in list)
Real PAM service toggle against /etc/pam.d (list detected services -> enable login -> verify pam_namtor.so block inserted -> disable -> verify removed)
Real authentication against a running PAM stack (login/sudo/su/polkit with pam_namtor.so enabled -> face match -> success; daemon down -> password fallback)
High-impact confirmation dialog rendered on a real display for login/sudo/su/polkit services
Accessibility verification with a real screen reader and keyboard-only navigation
Persistence across session restart and reboot
Polkit prompt rendered on a real desktop for org.namtor.configure-pam
The same binary rendering correctly on a non-GNOME desktop (Plasma, Xfce, sway), which is the claim that replaced the deleted per-desktop UIs

test_suite.note: Was 63 passed at the previous revision. The gate had drifted to 13 failures, all invisible because no workflow ran this script. Each per-test check now consults the whole-crate test inventory instead of grepping one test target, because a filter matching nothing prints 'test result: ok. 0 passed' and so reported a renamed test as a failing one.
